title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Non-Executive Directors and Senior Executives of the Company (including the Managing Director), as determined by the Board from time to time. All substantive prohibitions (inside information, prohibited periods, short-term dealing, short selling, use of Company securities as loan security) apply to this tier without differentiation.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Non-Executive Directors, including the Managing Director; distinguished only for pre-trade notification (to the Chairman or Chairman of the Audit Committee or the MD, and either the CFO or Company Secretary) and for routing of exceptional-circumstances clearance requests.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Senior Executives excluding the Managing Director; distinguished only for pre-trade notification (to the Company Secretary, CFO or MD) and for routing of exceptional-circumstances clearance requests (to the MD).

tiers.name: Closely Connected Persons and Entities
tiers.description: Family members whose financial affairs are controlled by the KMP, and companies, trusts and entities controlled by the KMP.

definitions.hedging_definition: using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities (hedging)

windows.end_anchor: the calendar day after the Company's announcement of its interim financial results
the calendar day after the Company's announcement of its final financial results

windows.start_anchor: start of the pricing period for any capital management event
windows.end_anchor: end of the pricing period for that capital management event

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose other periods when KMP are prohibited from dealing because inside information may exist; the policy does not state whether these are announced or confidential.

rules.detail: The policy has no definitions section and never defines 'dealing' or 'the Company's securities' to state whether derivatives (exchange-traded or OTC) over Company securities are covered; only ordinary buying/selling is discussed.

The Company states it has no equity-based remuneration schemes and therefore no need for restrictions on KMP using financial products to hedge unvested Company securities. Hedging of ordinary (vested) holdings is not separately addressed and would only be constrained, if at all, via the secured-loan ban in 2.5 or the general prohibited-period rules if the hedge is a dealing.
rules.evidence: The Company does not operate any equity-based remuneration schemes. As such, there is no need to have restrictions in place to prohibit KMP from using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities (hedging).

rules.detail: Monetisation structures (prepaid forwards, equity swaps) are not named or otherwise addressed.
Outright ban on short-selling of the Company's securities, with no carve-out.
rules.evidence: KMP must not engage in short-selling of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named; a short CFD would in substance fall within the short-selling ban (2.4), but the point is not addressed expressly.

KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements, with no vesting or approval carve-out; KMP must also use best endeavours to avoid conflicts arising from margin or other loans over other securities.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: The prohibition on using the Company's securities as security for 'margin lending arrangements or other loans' extends the encumbrance ban beyond classic broker margin facilities to any charge or pledge over the shares that secures a loan.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: The ban is not limited to margin lending; 'or other loans' sweeps in any secured financing arrangement in respect of the Company's securities, with no exemption authority.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: No fixed holding period; an intention-based standard requiring dealings for investment purposes and holding for a reasonable period rather than active, prompt or repetitive trading.
rules.evidence: KMP must not deal in the Company's securities for short-term purposes. Dealings in the Company's securities must be undertaken for investment purposes and not for trading, that is, the intention in undertaking transactions should be to hold the Company's securities for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling them.

clearance.approver: Chairman or the Chairman of the Audit Committee or the MD, and either the CFO or Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: The Chairman or the Chairman of the Audit Committee or the MD and either the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) or Company Secretary must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Directors (including the MD) in the Company's securities.
The Company Secretary, CFO or MD must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Senior Executives (excluding the MD) in the Company's securities.

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Audit Committee (if the requester is the Chairman) or the Chairman (if another Director, or in his absence the Chairman of the Audit Committee or the MD)
clearance.evidence: Approval will be given in writing (including via email) and copied to the Company Secretary who shall maintain a record of all such approvals. Such approval will be for 5 business days beginning the business day after approval is given.

clearance.approver: MD (or in his absence the Chairman or Chairman of the Audit Committee)
clearance.evidence: by Senior Executives (excluding the MD) to the MD (or in his absence the Chairman or Chairman of the Audit Committee). Approval will be given in writing (including via email) ... for 5 business days beginning the business day after approval is given.

short_term.basis: no fixed period; investment-purpose test judged against active, prompt or repetitive buying and selling
short_term.evidence: the intention in undertaking transactions should be to hold the Company's securities for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling them.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of Company securities already held by the KMP into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the KMP is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme or arrangement (other than a scheme only investing in the Company's securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a KMP is a trustee, trading in the Company's securities by that trust provided the KMP is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the KMP
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer

dealing under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the securityholders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend reinvestment plan, a dividend substitution share plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
where the beneficial interest in the relevant Company security does not change
transactions conducted between a KMP and their spouse, civil partner, child, step-child or other close family member.

A KMP who is not in possession of inside information may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) the Company's securities when they would otherwise be prohibited by this policy from doing so if they are in severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances apply.

A circumstance will be considered exceptional if the KMP in question is required by a court order to transfer or sell the Company's securities or there is some other overriding legal requirement for them to do so.

exemption_authority: Exceptional Circumstances relief (severe financial difficulty or court order) may permit a sale only, not a purchase, during a prohibited period, approved via the routing in 7.3; the Company may need to notify ASX of the existence of exceptional circumstances (5.4). No exemption authority exists for the margin lending/secured loan ban (2.5), the short-selling ban (2.4) or the short-term dealing rule (2.3).

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured loans not limited to margin lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This bans any bank loan secured over the collared shares outright, not just broker margin facilities, so the funded leg of a collar cannot be structured under this policy regardless of tenor or approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company does not operate any equity-based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no unvested KMP shareholding to consider; any collar would be over ordinary, already-vested shares, so the vesting-state distinction in the schema is largely moot for MIR.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP must use all reasonable endeavours to ensure that, if they have a reportable interest in the Company's securities as defined by the ASX Listing Rules and Corporations Act due to a relationship with a third party, that third party complies with this policy as if it were a KMP.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan booked through a related third party (trust, SMSF, spouse) does not escape the secured-financing ban if the KMP has a reportable interest in the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A KMP ... may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) the Company's securities when they would otherwise be prohibited ... if they are in severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances apply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even absent the secured-financing ban, entering a collar (writing a call, buying a put) during a prohibited period could not rely on the exceptional-circumstances carve-out, which only ever authorises an outright sale.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no definition of dealing or securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because 'dealing' and 'the Company's securities' are never formally defined, whether an OTC put/call over MIR shares is caught at all is genuinely ambiguous, creating interpretive risk for a bank counterparty independent of the express secured-financing ban.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable under this policy. Clause 2.5 prohibits KMP from using the Company's securities as security for 'margin lending arrangements or other loans', a broad ban that plainly catches a bank loan secured over the collared shares, with no clearance, tier or vesting carve-out and no exemption authority. The put and call legs themselves are not expressly addressed: the policy has no definitions section for 'dealing' or 'the Company's securities', so coverage of OTC derivatives is ambiguous, though in substance such trades would likely be treated as dealings subject to the prohibited-period rules and the pre-trade notification obligations to the Chairman/Audit Committee Chair/MD and CFO or Company Secretary (Directors) or Company Secretary/CFO/MD (Senior Executives). Since MIR has no equity-based incentive scheme, all holdings are ordinary vested shares, so the vesting-state question is not material. Even where a prohibited-period exception could otherwise apply, the Exceptional Circumstances relief is limited to an outright sale, not to entering a derivative or financing arrangement, so it offers no route around the secured-financing ban.
